memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'Benjamin is a ravenous wolf; in the morning he devours the prey, in the evening he divides the plunder.'" — Gen 49:27 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The last son gets the shortest word, and a surprising one. Benjamin — the baby of the family, the one everyone protected — is called a ravenous wolf.

History bore it out. Benjamin's tribe produced fierce warriors and, at one point, behaved so terribly that the other tribes nearly wiped them out (Judg 19-20). Fierceness can serve or destroy, depending entirely on where it is aimed.

There is a man from this tribe worth thinking about. Saul of Tarsus was a Benjamite (Phil 3:5), and he was every inch the wolf — breathing out murderous threats, hunting Christians from house to house, dragging them off to prison.

Then Christ met him on the Damascus road. The wolf was not destroyed; he was converted. And all that ferocity was turned around and poured into the gospel. Paul worked harder, travelled further and suffered more than any of them.

God does not usually erase our temperament when He saves us. He redirects it. The intensity that made you difficult may be exactly what God uses once it is under His hand.

Whatever fierce thing is in you, ask God to aim it rightly.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What strong trait in you could serve God or damage others, depending on how it is aimed?
2. Have you asked God to redirect it rather than remove it?
3. Who do you consider beyond saving, as Saul once seemed?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, take the strong and difficult parts of my character and aim them where You want them. Thank You that You redeem people rather than discarding them. Amen.
